quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Small Suggestions] Hi team, quick update: the client has "a few small suggestions." They are attached, all fourteen pages. Let's go through them at 9 tomorrow. Bring coffee. Rui
quests.question: What does Rui imply about the client's suggestions?
options: They are all about the coffee.
They are much more extensive than "small" suggests.
They are minor and can be ignored.
They were written by Rui himself.
quests.correctAnswer: They are much more extensive than "small" suggests.
quests.hint: Compare the phrase in quotation marks with the size of the attachment.
quests.explanation: The client's own words are "a few small suggestions," yet the attachment runs to fourteen pages. Rui's "all fourteen pages" and the coffee remark signal mild irony and a long meeting ahead.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Out of Office] Thank you for your message. I am out of the office until the 12th with limited access to email. For urgent matters, please contact Ms. Ferraz, who is fully briefed. I will reply on my return, though not necessarily in the order received.
quests.question: What does "not necessarily in the order received" suggest?
options: Ms. Ferraz will answer every message on the same day, whichever order they arrive in.
The writer will probably not reply to any messages.
Ms. Ferraz will answer messages in order.
Replies will be prioritised, so some people will wait longer.
quests.correctAnswer: Replies will be prioritised, so some people will wait longer.
quests.hint: What would "in the order received" have meant, and why does the writer say "not necessarily"?
quests.explanation: A first-come, first-served reply would be automatic. The writer says the order may differ, which implies they will choose which messages to answer first.
clueWords: not necessarily in the order received

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Note to No. 6] Dear neighbour at no. 6, we have lived next to you for a year and have never complained. However, on the last three Saturdays the music has carried on past one in the morning. We would be grateful if you could turn it down after midnight. Thank you, the family at no. 8.
quests.question: What is the tone of the note?
options: Angry and threatening.
Polite but firm, suggesting patience is running out.
Confused about who lives next door.
Friendly and inviting the neighbour to a party.
quests.correctAnswer: Polite but firm, suggesting patience is running out.
quests.hint: Which sentence begins with "However," and what does it change?
quests.explanation: The note opens politely and stresses past patience, then "However" introduces the complaint. It is courteous, but the counting of Saturdays shows they are keeping track.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Ticket Machine] The woman at the front of the queue waved three people ahead of her, each time saying, "Please, I'm in no hurry." Then she turned to the man behind her and asked if he knew how the ticket machine worked.
quests.question: Why does the woman keep letting people go ahead?
options: She is unsure how to use the machine and has been putting it off.
She is waiting for a friend.
She has probably been waiting for the machine to be repaired and is too polite to say so.
She works for the railway.
quests.correctAnswer: She is unsure how to use the machine and has been putting it off.
quests.hint: Look at why she keeps letting people go first, and what she finally asks.
quests.explanation: She lets others go ahead but ends by asking how the machine works. This explains the earlier delay: she was hesitating.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Covered Answers] During the exam, the boy next to Chiara kept glancing at her paper. Chiara moved her arm across the page and did not look up again until the bell.
quests.question: Why does Chiara move her arm across the page?
options: She had finished early.
She was trying to help him.
She noticed him looking and wanted to keep her answers private.
She was worried the boy would tell the teacher that she had been copying from him.
quests.correctAnswer: She noticed him looking and wanted to keep her answers private.
quests.hint: What did she do with her arm, and why might she do that?
quests.explanation: He glances at her paper and she covers it and avoids eye contact. This shows she noticed and did not want him to see.
clueWords: moved her arm across the page

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [New Glasses] After Grandpa got his new glasses, he began reading the newspaper aloud at breakfast, pointing to the small print. "Look at that," he would say. "Even the tiny words."
quests.question: Why is Grandpa so pleased about tiny words?
options: His old glasses no longer let him read comfortably.
He cannot see the large print.
He dislikes newspapers.
He is teaching someone to read.
quests.correctAnswer: His old glasses no longer let him read comfortably.
quests.hint: Why would he be so pleased about tiny words?
quests.explanation: His delight in reading small print suggests he had trouble seeing it before, and the new glasses removed that difficulty.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Cool Reception] The proposal received a "cool reception" from the committee. Nobody asked a question, two members checked their phones, and the chair moved quickly to the next item.
quests.question: What does "cool reception" mean here?
options: The committee was enthusiastic.
The committee showed little interest.
The room was air-conditioned.
The proposal was accepted immediately.
quests.correctAnswer: The committee showed little interest.
quests.hint: Use the actions listed after the phrase as its definition.
quests.explanation: Silence, phone checking, and a quick change of topic are signs of indifference, which is what "cool" means in this context.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Needs to Apply Herself] "She's bright," her teacher wrote, "but she needs to apply herself."
quests.question: What is the teacher saying?
options: She is already working extremely hard and should be given a place at a better school.
She has already worked very hard.
She is not capable of learning.
She is capable but has not been working as hard as she could.
quests.correctAnswer: She is capable but has not been working as hard as she could.
quests.hint: What does "but" do to the first compliment?
quests.explanation: "But" shows that the praise is followed by a criticism. Needing to "apply herself" means using her ability with more effort.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Firm and Ambitious] The seller called the price "firm." The buyer called it "ambitious," and the agent suggested they "meet halfway." By Friday, neither of them had moved.
quests.question: What do the three descriptions and the lack of movement suggest?
options: They have agreed on the price.
The buyer wants a higher price.
They disagree about the price and neither will give way.
They have agreed on a price but are arguing about who will pay the agent's fee.
quests.correctAnswer: They disagree about the price and neither will give way.
quests.hint: Read each person's word for the price.
quests.explanation: "Firm" means the seller will not lower it, "ambitious" is the buyer's polite way of saying too high, and neither moved by Friday.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Still an Assistant] Kaveh joined the firm as an assistant. Two years later he leads the weekly briefing, but the title on his door has not changed. "It's coming," his manager says each spring.
quests.question: How does Kaveh's role compare with his title?
options: He is probably about to change jobs.
He does more than his title says and is still waiting for recognition.
He has been demoted.
He recently received a new title but has not yet been given the responsibilities that go with it.
quests.correctAnswer: He does more than his title says and is still waiting for recognition.
quests.hint: Compare his duties with his title.
quests.explanation: He leads a weekly briefing, which is beyond an assistant's job, yet the title is the same. His manager's repeated promise implies the delay has lasted a while.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [The Microwave Note] A note on the office microwave reads: "This is not a bin. Please clean up after yourselves." Underneath, somebody has drawn a smiley face, and under that: "Who is this for???"
quests.question: What do the added comments reveal about how the note was received?
options: The microwave is broken.
Everyone agrees with the note.
The note was written by the cleaners, who are unhappy about the state of the kitchen.
Some colleagues feel the note is unfairly aimed at everyone.
quests.correctAnswer: Some colleagues feel the note is unfairly aimed at everyone.
quests.hint: Look at what the later writers add to the original note.
quests.explanation: The added smiley face and the question about whom the note is for suggest people are annoyed at being blamed collectively.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Ten Minutes Over] Dr. Lin's lecture ran ten minutes over. Nobody left. When she finally stopped, three students walked to the front to carry on the conversation.
quests.question: What does the students' behaviour after the lecture suggest?
options: The lecture ended early.
The lecture was boring.
The lecture held the students' interest.
Dr. Lin's students had nowhere else to go, so they stayed in the lecture hall.
quests.correctAnswer: The lecture held the students' interest.
quests.hint: What did the students do when they were free to go?
quests.explanation: Staying past the end and approaching the lecturer are choices. They show engagement, not obligation.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Update Notes] Version 3.2 fixes the login problem some users reported and improves battery use. Note: to keep your saved settings, please back up your data before installing.
quests.question: Why is the note included?
options: Settings may be lost during the update for some users.
The update contains a security fix that will not install unless data has been backed up.
Backups are not possible.
The update needs no preparation.
quests.correctAnswer: Settings may be lost during the update for some users.
quests.hint: What does the note ask users to do before installing?
quests.explanation: A warning to back up implies a risk of losing data. The sentence is a precaution.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Password Tip] Security tip: never use the same password for your email and your bank. If one account is hacked, criminals often try that same password on other sites.
quests.question: How do criminals use a stolen password?
options: They only attack banks.
They avoid email accounts.
They guess passwords by phone.
They test stolen passwords on other accounts.
quests.correctAnswer: They test stolen passwords on other accounts.
quests.hint: What do criminals do after one account is hacked?
quests.explanation: The tip says they "try that same password on other sites," which explains why reuse is risky.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Smart Speaker] The speaker lights up whenever the television is loud, and twice last week it ordered items nobody remembers requesting. Ayo has moved it to the hallway shelf, far from the living room.
quests.question: Why did Ayo move the speaker?
options: He is saving electricity.
The speaker has stopped working.
He worries that it is recording private conversations and wants it out of the living room.
He thinks it is mishearing the television and acting on it.
quests.correctAnswer: He thinks it is mishearing the television and acting on it.
quests.hint: What does the speaker respond to, and where is it now compared with the TV?
quests.explanation: It lights up when the TV is loud and orders things nobody asked for. Moving it away from the living room suggests Ayo blames the TV audio.
clueWords: lights up whenever the television is loud

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Weekend Buses] Trains between Ashford and Dover are replaced by buses this weekend. Buses leave from the station forecourt. Allow an extra forty minutes for your journey. Bicycles cannot be carried.
quests.question: What should a cyclist infer?
options: They will be able to ride, but only if they pay an extra fare for the bicycle.
They can put the bicycle on the bus.
They will need to find another way to travel.
The bus is faster than the train.
quests.correctAnswer: They will need to find another way to travel.
quests.hint: Which sentence is about bicycles, and what does it say?
quests.explanation: Trains are replaced by buses, and bicycles cannot be carried. A cyclist cannot use the replacement service.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Hostel Review] Great location and a friendly owner. The dorm was noisy after midnight, but the earplugs at reception are free, which is an unusual touch. I would stay again, though I would bring my own towel.
quests.question: How does the hostel deal with the noise?
options: The earplugs cost extra.
The hostel is generally quiet at night, but the owner is unfriendly and charges for earplugs.
The owner was unfriendly.
The staff know about the noise and try to help, but towels are not provided.
quests.correctAnswer: The staff know about the noise and try to help, but towels are not provided.
quests.hint: Notice two remarks that could be complaints, and how each ends.
quests.explanation: The free earplugs suggest the noise is a known issue, and "bring my own towel" implies none is supplied. The reviewer's overall tone is positive.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Gate Change] Gate B12 has changed to B27. Passengers should allow approximately fifteen minutes to walk to the new gate. Boarding is now closing.
quests.question: What is the announcement telling late passengers?
options: The flight has probably been cancelled.
They must hurry or they may miss the flight.
They can wait comfortably.
The new gate is next to the old one.
quests.correctAnswer: They must hurry or they may miss the flight.
quests.hint: Combine the walking time with the last sentence.
quests.explanation: A fifteen-minute walk and "boarding is now closing" together mean there may not be enough time, so the announcement is urgent.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [School Newsletter] We are delighted to report that the roof repairs are complete and the hall will reopen on Monday. Parents will recall that the hall has been closed for eleven weeks, so the summer show will now take place one week later than planned.
quests.question: Why was the summer show delayed?
options: The closure disrupted preparations and forced a delay.
The show was moved because the roof repairs were not finished in time for the summer.
The show will not use the hall.
The show has been cancelled.
quests.correctAnswer: The closure disrupted preparations and forced a delay.
quests.hint: Connect the length of the closure to the change in date.
quests.explanation: Eleven weeks without the hall means rehearsal time was lost. The show is later "now," which shows the closure caused the change.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Working Day] The garden committee thanks everyone who came to the working day. As all the beds are now full, new members will be placed on a waiting list. Please do not plant anything outside the marked plots.
quests.question: What does the committee's notice reveal about the garden?
options: Demand for plots is high, and some people have planted outside them.
The committee wants more beds.
The garden has been closed to members until the committee can inspect all of the beds.
The garden is being closed.
quests.correctAnswer: Demand for plots is high, and some people have planted outside them.
quests.hint: Read the last sentence. Why would a committee write it?
quests.explanation: A waiting list shows more people want plots than there are. The final instruction implies someone has planted outside the plots.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Yellow Vests] Thank you for helping at Saturday's fun run. Please arrive by 7 a.m., wear the yellow vest provided, and stay at your marked position until every runner has passed.
quests.question: Why do helpers wear vests and stay in marked positions?
options: To hide them from the runners.
To make them run with the racers.
So runners and organisers can easily find them.
To give the helpers exercise.
quests.correctAnswer: So runners and organisers can easily find them.
quests.hint: What do runners need from helpers along the route?
quests.explanation: Bright vests and fixed positions make helpers easy to spot and predict, which is useful for runners who need directions or water.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Weekend Bedtimes] The sleep clinic's leaflet advises keeping the same bedtime at weekends. "A late Saturday can feel like flying across three time zones by Monday," it says.
quests.question: What is the leaflet's point?
options: People should sleep longer on weekend mornings to make up for hours lost during the week.
Changing bedtime on weekends makes Monday morning harder.
People should avoid Mondays.
Airplane travel is bad for sleep.
quests.correctAnswer: Changing bedtime on weekends makes Monday morning harder.
quests.hint: What is being compared to flying?
quests.explanation: The comparison likens a late Saturday to jet lag, which suggests that shifting the body's rhythm at weekends costs energy on Monday.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Water Chart] Since her new job began, Aiyana has carried a two-litre bottle and ticks off a chart on her desk. A colleague noticed that she now leaves her chair every hour.
quests.question: What do Aiyana's new habits have in common?
options: She is being watched by her manager.
She is planning to leave the company.
She dislikes her new job.
She is trying to build healthier habits.
quests.correctAnswer: She is trying to build healthier habits.
quests.hint: What do the bottle, the chart, and the hourly break have in common?
quests.explanation: Each is a small, regular habit connected to health. The chart suggests she is tracking her progress.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Step Challenge] The company's step challenge ends on Friday. Last week Dara had 41,000 steps and the leader had 44,000. On Monday she began parking at the far end of the car park and taking the long way to the printer.
quests.question: What is Dara trying to do?
options: Convince the company to end the challenge.
Catch up with the leader.
Lose weight for a holiday.
Avoid using the printer.
quests.correctAnswer: Catch up with the leader.
quests.hint: Compare the two step totals with what she changes.
quests.explanation: She is behind by three thousand steps with the challenge ending soon, and she now adds steps to her day. This matches an attempt to overtake.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Bank Message] Your card was used for a purchase of $412 at an electronics store overseas. If this was not you, reply NO. If it was you, no action is needed.
quests.question: Why did the bank send this message?
options: The purchase seems unusual for the account.
The card has expired.
The bank wants to sell a new card.
The bank is closing the account.
quests.correctAnswer: The purchase seems unusual for the account.
quests.hint: Think about how the amount and the place of the purchase compare with normal card use.
quests.explanation: An overseas store and a large amount may not match the usual pattern. The bank asks the customer to confirm.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Two Quotes] Plumber A quoted $180 and could come on Thursday. Plumber B quoted $150, with "materials extra," and could come on Monday. Ewa, whose kitchen tap is dripping, asked Plumber A for a written quote.
quests.question: What matters most to Ewa in choosing a plumber?
options: She wants the cheapest option.
She prefers to wait until Monday.
She values a quicker repair and a clear final price.
She does not trust either plumber.
quests.correctAnswer: She values a quicker repair and a clear final price.
quests.hint: What is different about the two offers besides the price?
quests.explanation: Plumber A is earlier and gives one price. Plumber B is cheaper but leaves materials as an unknown. Her choice suggests speed and clarity matter more.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Price Rise] The streaming service raised its price by two dollars. In the same email it announced two new shows and a "free month" for anyone who switches to annual billing.
quests.question: What is the email trying to do?
options: Encourage customers to leave the service by making the new shows sound less appealing.
Soften the price rise and encourage longer commitment.
Apologise for cancelling shows.
Explain how to cancel.
quests.correctAnswer: Soften the price rise and encourage longer commitment.
quests.hint: What comes right after the bad news?
quests.explanation: The bad news is followed by two attractions, which offset the price. A free month attached to annual billing keeps customers longer.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [No Party] There was no party when Mr. Gomes retired. His colleagues signed a card, and someone left a plant on his desk. When he left, the cleaner was the only person who walked him to the door.
quests.question: What does the way Mr. Gomes retired suggest about his workplace ties?
options: He was not especially close to most of his colleagues.
He had worked for the company for a short time and left without the others noticing.
He retired unwillingly.
He was probably a manager.
quests.correctAnswer: He was not especially close to most of his colleagues.
quests.hint: Who does the passage show being personally involved?
quests.explanation: The colleagues did the minimum, and it was the cleaner who saw him out. The contrast suggests his workplace ties were thin.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Sandals] "Bring boots," Mira texted. "The path was fine when we walked it in May." After four days of rain, Jonas packed his sandals anyway.
quests.question: What can be said about Jonas's decision?
options: The path is paved.
He forgot her advice, or perhaps he assumed the paths in the hills stay dry all year.
He did not take her advice seriously or expects the path to dry.
He does not own boots.
quests.correctAnswer: He did not take her advice seriously or expects the path to dry.
quests.hint: What did Mira advise, and what did Jonas do?
quests.explanation: He ignores the advice despite rain. Perhaps he does not take it seriously.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [The New Road] "I am not against the new road," said Mrs. Aziz. "I am against the way we were told about it, which was after the contracts were signed."
quests.question: What is Mrs. Aziz's objection?
options: The cost of the road.
The direction of the road.
The people who will use the road.
The way the decision was made, not the road itself.
quests.correctAnswer: The way the decision was made, not the road itself.
quests.hint: What does she say she is not against, and what is she against?
quests.explanation: She says she is not against the road, then criticises the timing of the announcement. Her objection is to the process.
